To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anti-43 kDA antibody recognizes the pGlyBP, which has been cloned from rat brain, and that the purified 60 kDa pGlyBP binds glycine and glutamate and has high affinity glycine and glutamte binding sites.

we have cloned a cDNA for the 43 kDa subunit of a complex of proteins that bind strychnine-sensitive glycine, NMDAR and MK-801, and have isolated a 60 kD protein from rat brain synaptic membrane that binds strychnine- and D-serine-sensitive glycine and L-glutamate, and is recognized by antibodies to the 43 kD protein.
the anti-43 kD antibodies label a 60 KD protein in synaptic membranes, and that this protein can be purified from synaptic membranes by chromatography on 5,7-DKC- and 8-OHQ-derivatized matrices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and immunocharacterization of a synaptic membrane protein that is a candidate for the glycine-binding site of the glycine-NMDA receptor complex.
the identification of a synaptic membrane glycine-binding protein, pGyBP, that may be an important component of NMDA receptors.
the identification of a protein that is involved in the binding of glycine to the glycine site of NMDA receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 60kDa protein is pGlyBP and that pGlyBP is a glycine, glutamate, and TCP-binding protein.

the 55- 60 kDa synaptic membrane protein, isolated in the present study, is a member of the NMDA receptor complex, which binds glycine, glutamate, and MK801 with high affinity and glycine and R-(+)HA-966 with low affinity, and is the same protein described previously as a glycine-,glutamate- and thieylcycloheylpiperidine binding protein (pGlyBP) (Kumar et. al.
the anti-43 kD antibodies react strongly with the 60 kD protein in the brain synaptic membranes and the isolated 55-60kD protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 43 kD protein is a major constituent of the NMDAR, that this protein is a glycoprotein, that the 43 kDa protein is a subunit of the 60 kD protein, and that the 60kD protein is a sub-unit of the NMDA receptor.
we have cloned a cDNA for the 43 kDa protein and isolated the protein from brain synaptic membranes.
we have cloned the gene for a protein that is a component of the NMDA receptor complex and we have purified the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-43 kDA antibodies can be used to identify the 60 kDA protein in brain synaptic membranes.
the glycine binding protein is a 60 kD glycoprotein.
the glycine binding site of pGlyBP is not the same as the strychnine-sensitive glycine binding site that is associated with the NMDA receptor complex.
